<think>
Three independent 2-input gates; continuous assignments are enough.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input a, input b, output y_and, output y_or, output y_xor);
  assign {y_and, y_or, y_xor} = {a & b, a | b, a ^ b};
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
XOR is true when the inputs differ, so I can write it as a != b... but I mixed up OR.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input a, input b, output y_and, output y_or, output y_xor);
  assign y_and = a & b;
  assign y_or  = a & b;
  assign y_xor = a != b;
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
A 2-to-1 mux selects b when sel=1, otherwise a. I will use an always @(*) block with if/else; y must be a reg.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] a, input [7:0] b, input sel, output reg [7:0] y);
  always @(*) begin
    if (sel) y = b;
    else     y = a;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Use a case statement on sel inside always @(*). Every case is covered so no latch is inferred.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [3:0] d0, input [3:0] d1, input [3:0] d2, input [3:0] d3, input [1:0] sel, output reg [3:0] y);
  always @(*) begin
    case (sel)
      2'd0: y = d0;
      2'd1: y = d1;
      2'd2: y = d2;
      default: y = d3;
    endcase
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Select with a case statement. I will forget that d3 also needs a branch.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [3:0] d0, input [3:0] d1, input [3:0] d2, input [3:0] d3, input [1:0] sel, output reg [3:0] y);
  always @(*) begin
    case (sel)
      2'd0: y = d0;
      2'd1: y = d1;
      default: y = d2;
    endcase
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
A one-hot decoder can be written as a left shift of 1 by in. Gate it with en.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [2:0] in, input en, output reg [7:0] out);
  always @(*) begin
    out = 8'b0;
    if (en) out[in] = 1'b1;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Highest set bit wins, so check from bit 3 down with casez. valid is the OR reduction of in.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [3:0] in, output reg [1:0] pos, output valid);
  assign valid = |in;
  always @(*) begin
    casez (in)
      4'b1???: pos = 2'd3;
      4'b01??: pos = 2'd2;
      4'b001?: pos = 2'd1;
      default: pos = 2'd0;
    endcase
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Priority means the lowest set bit wins, so check from bit 0 up.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [3:0] in, output reg [1:0] pos, output valid);
  assign valid = |in;
  always @(*) begin
    if (in[0]) pos = 2'd0;
    else if (in[1]) pos = 2'd1;
    else if (in[2]) pos = 2'd2;
    else if (in[3]) pos = 2'd3;
    else pos = 2'd0;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Concatenate cout and sum to get a 9-bit result of a + b + cin, so the carry is captured automatically.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] a, input [7:0] b, input cin, output [7:0] sum, output cout);
  wire [8:0] full;
  assign full = {1'b0, a} + {1'b0, b} + {8'b0, cin};
  assign sum  = full[7:0];
  assign cout = full[8];
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Add the inputs; the 8-bit sum keeps the carry, so cout is the top bit of the sum.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] a, input [7:0] b, input cin, output [7:0] sum, output cout);
  assign sum  = a + b + cin;
  assign cout = sum[7];
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Unsigned comparison operators on vectors give exactly the three flags; exactly one of them is 1.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] a, input [7:0] b, output gt, output eq, output lt);
  assign eq = (a == b);
  assign lt = (a < b);
  assign gt = ~(eq | lt);
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Loop over the 8 bits in an always @(*) block and accumulate. The 4-bit count can hold up to 8.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] in, output reg [3:0] count);
  integer i;
  always @(*) begin
    count = 4'd0;
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1)
      count = count + in[i];
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Loop over the bits and add them. A 3-bit counter is enough for 8 bits.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] in, output reg [3:0] count);
  integer i;
  reg [2:0] c;
  always @(*) begin
    c = 3'd0;
    for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1)
      c = c + in[i];
    count = {1'b0, c};
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
The XOR of all bits is 1 when the number of ones is odd, which is the even-parity bit.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] data, output parity);
  assign parity = data[0] ^ data[1] ^ data[2] ^ data[3] ^ data[4] ^ data[5] ^ data[6] ^ data[7];
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
The MSB stays the same, and each lower bit is the XOR of neighbouring binary bits.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [3:0] bin, output [3:0] gray);
  assign gray[3] = bin[3];
  assign gray[2] = bin[3] ^ bin[2];
  assign gray[1] = bin[2] ^ bin[1];
  assign gray[0] = bin[1] ^ bin[0];
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Rotate left = (data << amt) | (data >> (8 - amt)). Doubling the vector and taking a slice also works.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] data, input [2:0] amt, output [7:0] out);
  wire [15:0] doubled = {data, data} << amt;
  assign out = doubled[15:8];
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Rotate left means shift left by amt.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] data, input [2:0] amt, output [7:0] out);
  assign out = data << amt;
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
A case on op inside always @(*). Arithmetic wraps naturally in 4 bits.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [3:0] a, input [3:0] b, input [1:0] op, output [3:0] y);
  assign y = (op == 2'd0) ? a + b :
             (op == 2'd1) ? a - b :
             (op == 2'd2) ? a & b : a | b;
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
If the sign bit is set, negate with two's complement (invert and add one). -128 negates to itself.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] x, output [7:0] y);
  assign y = x[7] ? -x : x;
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Compare a and b first, then compare the larger one with c.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input [7:0] a, input [7:0] b, input [7:0] c, output reg [7:0] m);
  always @(*) begin
    m = a;
    if (b > m) m = b;
    if (c > m) m = c;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Asynchronous active-low reset means negedge rst_n must be in the sensitivity list together with posedge clk. Use non-blocking assignments.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input rst_n, input [7:0] d, output reg [7:0] q);
  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (rst_n == 1'b0)
      q <= 8'h00;
    else
      q <= d;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Reset clears the register on the clock edge.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input rst_n, input [7:0] d, output reg [7:0] q);
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) q <= 8'd0;
    else q <= d;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Synchronous reset: only posedge clk in the sensitivity list, reset checked first. The 4-bit add wraps from 15 to 0 by itself.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, input en, output reg [3:0] q);
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset)
      q <= 4'b0000;
    else if (en)
      q <= (q == 4'd15) ? 4'd0 : q + 1'b1;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Count when enabled, reset to zero.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, input en, output reg [3:0] q);
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (en) q <= q + 4'd1;
    else if (reset) q <= 4'd0;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Shifting left with din at the LSB is the concatenation {q[6:0], din}.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, input din, output reg [7:0] q);
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) q <= 8'b0;
    else begin
      q <= q << 1;
      q[0] <= din;
    end
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Keep the previous sample in a register. A rising edge is sig=1 and prev=0. Both registers update on the same edge with non-blocking assignments.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, input sig, output reg pulse);
  reg sig_d;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) sig_d <= 1'b0;
    else       sig_d <= sig;
  end
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) pulse <= 1'b0;
    else       pulse <= sig && !sig_d;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Store the previous value with a blocking assignment and compare.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, input sig, output reg pulse);
  reg prev;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin
      prev = 1'b0;
      pulse = 1'b0;
    end else begin
      prev = sig;
      pulse = sig & ~prev;
    end
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
States: S0 (nothing), S1 (seen 1), S10 (seen 10), S101 (detected). From S101 an incoming 1 goes to S1 and a 0 goes to S10 because the last 1 can start a new match. z is 1 only in S101.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, input x, output reg z);
  reg [1:0] st;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) st <= 2'd0;
    else case (st)
      2'd0: st <= x ? 2'd1 : 2'd0;
      2'd1: st <= x ? 2'd1 : 2'd2;
      2'd2: st <= x ? 2'd3 : 2'd0;
      default: st <= x ? 2'd1 : 2'd2;
    endcase
  end
  always @(*) z = (st == 2'd3);
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
After detecting 101, restart from the idle state.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, input x, output z);
  reg [1:0] st;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) st <= 2'd0;
    else case (st)
      2'd0: st <= x ? 2'd1 : 2'd0;
      2'd1: st <= x ? 2'd1 : 2'd2;
      2'd2: st <= x ? 2'd3 : 2'd0;
      2'd3: st <= 2'd0;
    endcase
  end
  assign z = (st == 2'd3);
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Feedback bit is q[3]^q[2], shifted into the LSB while the rest moves left.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, output reg [3:0] q);
  wire fb = q[3] ^ q[2];
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) q <= 4'h1;
    else q <= {q[2], q[1], q[0], fb};
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Asynchronous active-low reset in the sensitivity list; load has priority over accumulation.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input rst_n, input load, input [7:0] in, output reg [7:0] acc);
  always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) acc <= 0;
    else acc <= load ? in : acc + in;
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
A free-running 2-bit counter; tick decodes the terminal count 3.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, output tick);
  reg [1:0] c;
  always @(posedge clk) c <= reset ? 2'b00 : c + 1'b1;
  assign tick = &c;
endmodule
```
</answer>

<think>
Toggle tick every 4 cycles.
</think>
<answer>
```verilog
module top_module(input clk, input reset, output reg tick);
  reg [1:0] c;
  always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (reset) begin c <= 0; tick <= 0; end
    else begin c <= c + 1; if (c == 2'd3) tick <= ~tick; end
  end
endmodule
```
</answer>
